{{Quote|These people lay ancestral claim to the Dune Sea, and if you are to pass, a toll is to be paid to them.|Boba Fett, on the Tusken Raiders|<ref name="The Tribes of Tatooine">{{BOBF|Chapter 2: The Tribes of Tatooine}}</ref>}}
'''Tusken Raiders''', less formally referred to as '''Sand People''' or simply as '''Tuskens''', were a nomadic [[Sentience|sentient]] [[species]] [[Homeworld|indigenous]] to the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]], where they were often hostile to local settlers. Tusken [[Youngling|children]] were called '''Uli-ah'''. The name of ''Tusken Raiders'' was acquired much later, due to a period of concerted attacks on the settlement called [[Fort Tusken]] around eight decades before [[19 BBY]].

One [[Unidentified Tusken Raider tribe|tribe]] captured the [[bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett]], but they accepted him into their tribe after he had proved his worth to them.

==Culture==
{{Quote|A moisture farm? Poor locals never stood a chance. The Sand People think all water is sacred and was promised to them.|Saponza to [[Saponza's partner|his partner]] after discovering a moisture farm ravaged by Tusken Raiders|<ref name="Commander">''[[Star Wars: Commander]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Tuskens-2015DarthVader25.png|thumb|left|250px|A group of Tusken raiders]]
Tusken Raiders were a [[species]] [[Homeworld|native]] to the [[desert]] [[Planet|world]] of [[Tatooine]]. Their homeworld's harsh environment resulted in them being extremely xenophobic and territorial of their native resources, often attacking the outskirts of smaller settlements such as [[Anchorhead]].<ref name="SWE" /> They viewed themselves as Tatooine's rightful inhabitants, and all non-native species as trespassers.<ref name="Chapter 5" /> The Sand People believed that all [[water]] was sacred and promised to them, resulting in them raiding [[moisture farm]]s set up by colonists.<ref name="Commander" /> Rare water wells, such as [[Gafsa]], were also sacred to Tuskens. An individual simply trespassing close to one of these water wells could provoke immediate violence.<ref name="CVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]''</ref> Additionally, Tusken Raiders harvested [[black melon]]s which grew in the [[Jundland Wastes]], providing them with a reliable source of [[milk]].<ref name="SW7">[[Star Wars (2015) 7|''Star Wars'' (2015) 7]]</ref> [[Worrt]]s, a [[Sentience|non-sentient]]<ref name="Beware">''[[Return of the Jedi: Beware the Power of the Dark Side!]]''</ref> species native to Tatooine,<ref name="RotJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> were considered a delicacy by the Tusken Raiders.<ref name="Worrt DB">{{Databank|worrt|Worrt}}</ref>

A nomadic culture,<ref name="Time of Death">{{StoryCite|story=Time of Death|book=From a Certain Point of View}}</ref> Tusken clan groups consisted of 20 to 30 individuals, and were led by clan leaders, tribal chiefs,<ref name="The Tribes of Tatooine" /> and warlords.<ref name="Commander" /> Tuskens traveled in single file to hide the number of individuals in their party.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> The culture of different tribes varied greatly, with some surviving by killing outsiders, while other tribes used more peaceful means.<ref name="The Tribes of Tatooine" /> The Sand People communicated in [[Tusken]], which could refer to their ordinary spoken language as well as a trade-based sign language employed when communicating with outsiders. At the age of 15, a Tusken became an adult, and the boys had to slay a [[krayt dragon]] and cut out the precious [[Krayt dragon pearl|pearl]] found in its stomach<ref name="Absolutely Everything You Need to Know" /> to gain their adult role in their tribe.<ref name="CVD" /> Tuskens inhabited encampments scattered across an area of the rocky Jundland Wastes known as [[The Needles]],<ref name="Absolutely Everything You Need to Know" /> which were guarded from intruders by vicious [[massiff]]s.<ref name="AotC">{{Film|II}}</ref>

[[File:ProjectileWeapons-GaG.png|thumb|right|250px|Three Tuskens firing their slugthrowers at a passing speeder.]]
[[Gender|Male]] Tusken Raiders were the warriors of their clans, often attacking vulnerable travelers that were unfortunate enough to wander through their territory.<ref name="SWJB" /> They wielded [[gaderffii stick]]s in combat, and used [[cycler rifle]]s to fire on vehicles they spotted.<ref name="SWE" /> Every Tusken warrior created their own gaderffii stick, making each one unique. Males wore rough wrappings and garments that provided protection and allowed ease of movement.<ref name="Absolutely Everything You Need to Know" /> Male Tuskens served as [[Soldier|warriors]], while females held a number of roles.<ref name="CVD" /> In some tribes, females could be distinguished by their elaborate jeweled masks with eye-slits and torso-covering sand-shrouds. Tusken children,<ref name="SWE" /> known as Uli-ah,<ref name="CVD" /> wore unisex cowls and simple cloaks,<ref name="SWE" /> and could not dress like males or females until they reached adulthood. All Sand People wore mouth grilles and eye coverings to retain moisture and keep sand out. However, their need to protect their bodies from Tatooine's weather grew into a taboo against exposing any part of their bodies in public. Because of this, Tuskens almost never unmasked themselves, even in front of one another. They were forbidden to remove their clothing in front of others except at [[Reproduction|childbirth]], on their wedding night, and at coming-of-age ceremonies.<ref name="Absolutely Everything You Need to Know" /> In addition, no outsider is known to have seen behind a Tusken's mask and lived.<ref name="CVD" />

Nearly impossible to mention one without the other,<ref name="Insider 221">{{InsiderCite|221|A Certain Point of View}}</ref> the Sand People and [[bantha]]s shared a close, almost mystical bond. During warrior initiation rites, a young Tusken was given a bantha<ref name="Bantha">{{SWE|characters|bantha|bantha}}</ref> matching their own gender<ref name="Absolutely Everything You Need to Know" /> and learned to care for it, with the pair becoming extremely close as the youth earned a place in its clan.<ref name="SWE" /> A rider and their bantha developed a great affinity, trust, and respect for each other.<ref name="Insider 221" /> When Sand People married, their banthas also mated, and, should its rider [[Death|die]], their bantha usually perished shortly after. If a bantha died before its rider, its remains were placed in a large graveyard, which was treated with great respect by Tuskens and other banthas.<ref name="Absolutely Everything You Need to Know" />

[[File:Cocky_WotF.png|thumb|left|250px|Tusken Raiders could be a hostile warrior race.]]
While the Tuskens were nominally hostile towards outsiders, one tribe did enter into an arrangement with the lawman [[Cobb Vanth]], the Sheriff of [[Freetown]]. Vanth and the animal tamer [[Malakili]] secured the Tuskens' protection by supplying water and a pearl from the belly of a krayt [[dragon]]. These Tuskens also shared Vanth's hostility towards criminal elements, especially [[Slavery|slavers]].<ref name="Empire's End">''[[Aftermath: Empire's End]]''</ref> [[Unidentified Tusken Raider tribe|Another tribe]] accepted [[bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett]] into their ranks when he had proved himself.<ref name="The Tribes of Tatooine" /> Indeed, many Tuskens were known to negotiate with outsiders, with [[bounty]] hunter [[Din Djarin]] knowing he could earn safe passage through Tusken land in exchange for a tribute.<ref name="Chapter 5">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 5: The Gunslinger}}</ref> Djarin also noted that Tuskens were known to always keep their word.<ref name="Chapter 9">{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 9: The Marshal}}</ref>

The Tusken tribe that accepted Boba Fett was in possession of a [[Horned gekko|gekko]] that was capable of crawling inside a host being's body and creating [[Dream|hallucinations]]. The lizard was used by the tribe to guide individuals on spiritual journeys. When Fett had such vision, he came across a [[Wortwood tree|wortwood]] [[tree]] in the desert, from which he broke a [[Wood|branch]] to forge [[Boba Fett's gaderffii stick|his own]] [[gaderffii stick]]. The tribe also had a tradition of dancing around a campfire. When members of the tribe died, their bodies and weapons were gathered and burnt at a funeral pyre.<ref name="The Tribes of Tatooine" />

The Tuskens had superstitions about various landmarks on Tatooine. For example, the Tuskens avoided [[Mushroom Mesa]] at all costs and always fired their blasters before passing through the [[B'Thazoshe Bridge]].<ref name="Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref>

==History==
===Historical activity===
{{Quote|There are many different Tusken tribes. Since the oceans dried, we have stayed hidden. Other tribes have survived by killing.|translated=1|The chieftain of the tribe to Boba Fett|<ref name="The Tribes of Tatooine" />}}
[[File:MateusManhaniniCover-TPM25.png|thumb|right|300px|The Sand People of Tatooine found ways to survive amongst the world's sandy dunes after the oceans dried.]]
When the [[ocean]]s of Tatooine dried<ref name="The Tribes of Tatooine" /> for unknown reasons,<ref name="Absolutely Everything You Need to Know" /> the Sand People, having scattered into many different tribes, elected to mostly stay hidden from outsiders and colonists on their world. Some tribes remained steadfast in keeping themselves hidden from outsiders. However, others became aggressive and focused on killing the outsiders they encountered.<ref name="The Tribes of Tatooine" />

Around eight [[Standard decade|decades]] prior to the [[Proclamation of the New Order|proclamation]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]<ref name="HC11">{{HelmetCollectionCite|11|Weapons & Uniforms}}</ref> in [[19 BBY]],<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> the settlement called [[Fort Tusken]] was established on the edge of the Badlands of the Jundland Wastes. It almost immediately faced attacks from the local Sand People. The settlers experienced considerable loss of life and goods, until they ultimately decided to abandon Fort Tusken. From that point on, the settlers of Tatooine referred to the Sand People as "Tusken Raiders."<ref name="HC11" /> At one point during the thirty-two [[Standard year|year]] long reign of the [[Thief|bandit]] [[Alkhara]],<ref name="217 POV">{{InsiderCite|217|A Certain Point of View}}</ref> the bandit hired<ref name="CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> a group of Tuskens and ordered them to wipe out a local [[garrison]] of [[Law enforcement agency|police]]. Alkhara then betrayed his Tusken allies and had them [[Death penalty|executed]]. Aklhara's plot and other ugly encounters between the Tuskens and Tatooine settlers created a bad relationship between both groups, with the settlers developing a poor perception of the "Sand People."<ref name="217 POV" />

===Pre-Clone Wars===
{{Quote|I…I killed them. I killed them all. They're dead, every single one of them. And not just the men, but the women and the children too. They're like animals, and I slaughtered them like animals. I hate them!|Anakin Skywalker|<ref name="AotC" />}}
[[File:Tuskens_canyon.png|thumb|left|250px|A group of Tusken Raiders camped out on the Canyon Dune Turn.]]
In [[32 BBY]], during the [[Boonta Eve Classic]], several Sand People camped out on [[Canyon Dune Turn]]. During the first lap, they took several pot shots at passing [[podracer]]s with their [[slugthrower]]s. Though initially unsuccessful, on the second lap a Tusken managed to shoot down the podracer of [[pilot]] [[Teemto Pagalies]], causing it to crash.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>

In [[22 BBY]], a month before the [[First Battle of Geonosis]], Sand People attacked the [[Lars homestead|Lars moisture farm]] and kidnapped [[Shmi Skywalker Lars]], whom they imprisoned and tortured. Her son, the [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], returned to Tatooine to [[Mission to rescue Shmi Skywalker Lars|rescue]] her, but after he found her in a [[Unidentified Tusken village|Tusken camp]], she died of her injuries. The vengeful Anakin proceeded to slaughter every nearby Tusken.<ref name="AotC" /> Following the massacre, the Tuskens began to fear Skywalker as a vengeful desert [[demon]], and began performing ritual sacrifices to ward him off,<ref name="Absolutely Everything You Need to Know" /> but they also came to learn of the connection between what had happened and the [[Lars family]], resulting in the Tusken Raiders holding a grudge towards them for Skywalker's actions.<ref name="Time of Death" />

===Age of the Empire===
{{Quote|I think we better get indoors. The Sand People are easily startled but they will soon be back, and in greater numbers.|Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="ANH" />}}
[[File:320-trivia-gallery-05_30adcc82.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Tusken Raiders destroy Ezra's ship.]]
In [[2 BBY]],<ref name="Twin Suns date">{{RebelsDate|320}}</ref> while searching for [[Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] on Tatooine, Padawan [[Ezra Bridger]] and [[C1-10P]] were ambushed by a group of Tusken Raiders, who succeeded in destroying their [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor|ship]] before being killed by the former [[Sith apprentice]] [[Maul]].<ref name="Twin Suns">{{Rebels|Twin Suns (episode)}}</ref>

Around two years later,<ref name="Twin Suns date" /> a young female Tusken Raider named [[Reirin]] who dreamed of proving herself to her people was active. She chafed at her clan's restrictions on women fighting, even though she was one of the best fighters in her clan. Eventually, Reirin left, having been hired by a trader in Mos Eisley to recover an item from a tribe of Jawas, in exchange for passage off Tatooine. She used the distraction of R5-D4's malfunction, after being purchased by Owen Lars and Luke Skywalker, to sneak aboard the sandcrawler.<ref name="Reirin">{{StoryCite|story=Reirin (short story)|book=From a Certain Point of View}}</ref>

Anakin's son [[Luke Skywalker|Luke]] was attacked by a<ref name="ANH" /> young Tusken named [[A'Koba]]<ref name="Rites">{{StoryCite|story=Rites|book=From a Certain Point of View}}</ref> after venturing from his homestead to retrieve [[R2-D2]].<ref name="ANH" /> A'Koba, joined by two other members of [[A'Yark's tribe]], [[A'Vor]] and [[A'Vor's twin|his twin]],<ref name="Rites" /> began to raid Skywalker's [[X-34 landspeeder]], but Obi-Wan Kenobi, who cloaked himself with his [[Jedi apparel|Jedi robes]], then warded off the Tuskens<ref name="ANH" /> by imitating the cry of a krayt dragon.<ref name="216 Nature">{{InsiderCite|216|Forces of Nature: The Wild Spaces and Wilder Creatures of the Star Wars Galaxy|Forces of Nature: The Wild Spaces and Wilder Creatures of the ''Star Wars'' Galaxy}}</ref> Before they attacked Skywalker, [[A'Yark]] had warned the three young Tuskens about Kenobi, believing him to be a powerful [[shaman]] whom the air itself obeyed. Upon seeing the cloaked figure, the three recognized him as the so-called shaman they had been warned of and fled.<ref name="Rites" /> After greeting R2 and Skywalker and recovering [[C-3PO]], Kenobi proceeded to bring them to his [[Ben Kenobi's home|home]], as he understood that the Tuskens would return in larger numbers.<ref name="ANH" /> Indeed, when A'Koba reunited with A'Yark, he wanted to go back with reinforcements. After advising caution, A'Yark let the three gather more Tuskens to return to the gorge, seeing it as part of a leadership rite.<ref name="Rites" />

[[File:DarthVaderSlaughtersTuskens-2015DarthVader1.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Vader slaughtering a village of Raiders.]]
Shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin]], Anakin, now the Sith Lord [[Darth]] Vader, slaughtered a [[Unidentified Tusken Raider village|village]] of Tuskens prior to his meeting with bounty hunters [[Boba Fett]] and [[Krrsantan]].<ref name="Vader 1">[[Darth Vader (2015) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 1]]</ref> Following the attack, a [[Unidentified Tusken Raider (destroyed village)|survivor]] showed other Tuskens the ruins of his village and the corpses of his people. These Tuskens then built a shrine to Vader and sacrificed the survivor.<ref name="Coda">{{StoryCite|story=Coda|book=Darth Vader (2015) 25}}</ref>

Sometime after, a Tusken known as the "[[Jundland General]]" led his people in a series of coordinated strikes against the colonists of Tatooine. However, he and his followers were crushed by a [[Tatooine rebel cell|group]] of [[Mercenary|mercenaries]] led by [[Saponza]] and [[Saponza's partner|his partner]].<ref name="Commander" />

The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] [[agent]] [[Gita]] went undercover as a Tusken Raider [[sniper]] named Urrr'k. While undercover, Gita was recruited by the [[Hidden Hand]]'s leader, [[Gwi]], to be part of a [[Beilert Valance's crew|team]] led by the [[cyborg]] [[bounty hunter]] [[Beilert Valance]] on a [[Hunt for Vader|hunt]] for the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]].<ref name="Target Vader 1">[[Target Vader 1|''Target Vader'' 1]]</ref> Although Valance suspected she was an imposter because Tusken Raiders don't leave Tatooine.<ref name="Target Vader 3">[[Target Vader 3|''Target Vader'' 3]]</ref>

===New Republic Era===
{{Quote|I know these people. They are brutal. But so is the Dune Sea. They've survived for thousands of years in these sands and they know the krayt dragon better than anyone here. They are raiders, it's true. But they also keep their word.|Din Djarin speaks of the Tuskens to the residents of Mos Pelgo|<ref name="Chapter 9" />}}
[[File:TuskenRaiderTribe-BoBFCh1.png|thumb|right|250px|Members of the clan that captured Boba Fett.]]
Following Commander Skywalker's [[Rescue of Han Solo|rescue]] of Captain [[Han Solo]] from [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba]] the [[Hutt]], a [[Unidentified Tusken Raider tribe|tribe]] of Tusken Raiders captured bounty hunter Boba Fett. They also captured a [[Unidentified Rodian prisoner|Rodian]]. When Fett attempted to escape, he was defeated by one of the raiders, though he began to earn their respect upon defeating a [[sand beast]].<ref name="Stranger in a Strange Land">{{BOBF|Chapter 1: Stranger in a Strange Land}}</ref> A [[Tusken warrior|warrior]] instructed Fett how to fight with a Gaderffii stick, and Fett taught members of the tribe how to use [[speeder bike]]s. Eventually, after leading the tribe into a [[Raid on a Pyke repulsortrain|victory]] against an interloping [[Pyke Syndicate]] [[Tatooine repulsor train|repulsortrain]] that had attacked the tribe on multiple occasions, Fett was inducted into the tribe. The Tuskens used a [[Horned gekko|gekko]] that crawled inside Fett's body, giving him a vision and making him walk in the desert, until he came across a [[Wortwood tree|Wortwood]] [[tree]], from which he broke a [[Wood|branch]] to forge his own gaderffii stick in a [[Gaderffii stick workshop]].<ref name="Tribes of Tatooine">{{BOBF|Chapter 2: The Tribes of Tatooine}}</ref> However, the tribe was [[Massacre of a Tusken Raider tribe|massacred]] some time later,<ref name="Chapter 3">{{BOBF|Chapter 3: The Streets of Mos Espa}}</ref> by the Pyke Syndicate, who painted the symbol of a speeder bike gang known as the [[Kintan Striders Gang|Kintan Striders]] to put the blame on them.<ref name="Chapter 7">{{BOBF|Chapter 7: In the Name of Honor}}</ref>

Prior to the [[Battle of Jakku]], the [[Sheriff]] of Freetown, Cobb Vanth, struck a deal with local Tusken Raiders to protect his settlement from criminal elements. Like Vanth's community, the Tuskens despised criminals particularly slavers. When the [[Red Key Raiders]] under [[crime lord]] [[Lorgan Movellan]] [[Skirmish in Freetown|captured]] Freetown, the Tusken tribe ambushed the criminals and liberated the town.<ref name="Empire's End" />

In [[9 ABY]], the [[Mandalorian]] Din Djarin reluctantly teamed up with rookie bounty hunter, [[Toro Calican]]. The two set out on [[speeder bike]]s across the Dune Sea to [[Hunt for Fennec Shand|capture]] the [[Master Assassin]] [[Fennec Shand]]. On their way to the target, they encountered some Tusken Raiders. The Mandalorian negotiated through [[Tusken Sign Language]] to allow them safe passage through their land. The Tuskens allowed this, in exchange for the rookie bounty hunter's [[binoculars]], which Djarin willingly gave to them in spite of Calican's objection.<ref name="Chapter 5" />

[[File:Krayt_dragon_pearl.png|thumb|left|250px|A Tusken Raider holding an enormous krayt dragon pearl.]]
Some time after, a group of Tuskens allied themselves with Djarin and Cobb Vanth to [[Mission to Tatooine (Din Djarin)|team up and take down]] a massive krayt dragon living nearby. Having studied the dragon's digestive cycle for generations, the Tusken Raiders attempted make the dragon sleep longer by feeding a bantha to it, but the animal devoured a Tusken instead. Being out of ideas how to handle the dragon, the group joined forces with the people of Freetown, now once again known as Mos Pelgo. In exchange for their collaboration, the Tuskens promised to not attack Mos Pelgo again unless one of the villagers broke the peace. The Tuskens were also promised the corpse and [[ichor]] from the dragon. To take down the beast, Vanth and his men contributed explosives and worked alongside the Tuskens, who set up [[ballista]]s. Despite several Tuskens being eaten by the dragon, the group succeeded in killing the beast when Djarin sprung their explosives. The Tuskens then butchered the carcass, with one member finding a pearl inside, which greatly excited the tribe.<ref name="Chapter 9" />

In [[34 ABY]], during his self-imposed [[Exile (punishment)|exile]] on [[Ahch-To]], the [[Jedi Master]] Luke Skywalker had a [[dream]] where he ignored [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa's]] message and never joined the rebellion. In his dream, two decades had passed since any Tusken Raider had been seen on his side of Anchorhead and that nothing was left of them except for bones. Luke noted that for some reason, it made him feel sad.<ref name="TLJ Novel">''[[Star Wars: The Last Jedi: Expanded Edition]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Sand_peoples_by_McQuarrie.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Tusken Raiders concept art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]].]]
The Tuskens appeared initially in the [[Adventures of the Starkiller, Episode I: The Star Wars|second draft]] of ''Star Wars: A New Hope'', as Imperial [[Spy|spies]] deployed as a [[platoon]] onto the surface of Tatooine to search for whatever had brought [[Deacon|Deak Starkiller]] to that planet. They appeared to be humanoid, with red eyes, and drove distinctive [[landspeeder]]s. They became a native people of Tatooine in the third draft.<ref name="The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film">''[[The Making of Star Wars: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film]]''</ref>

For the ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' episode "[[Twin Suns (episode)|Twin Suns]]," the Tusken Raiders were designed to not have flowing robes to save valuable time and resources in animation rendering.<ref name="Trivia">{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/twin-suns-trivia-gallery|text="Twin Suns" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 5}}</ref>

The Tusken Raiders' barking speech was inspired by the sound of donkeys and mules, used for carrying filming equipment to remote locations in Tunisia;<ref name="guide" /> those vocals echoed off the canyon rocks,<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/drawing-from-the-present-familiar-creatures-in-a-galaxy-far-far-away|text=Drawing from the Present: Familiar Creatures in a Galaxy Far, Far Away|int=Back from the Drawing Board|nolive=1}}</ref> sometimes creating a scary and chilling effect, and often ruined filming.<ref name="guide" /> Sound designer [[Ben Burtt]] used those recordings<ref name="Absolutely Everything You Need to Know" /> and edited along with other animal breathing and wheezing sounds to create the Tusken voices.<ref name="guide">[[Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide (real-life book)|''Galactic Phrase Book & Travel Guide'']]</ref>
